title: Ratify provenance+evidence mechanism + define countable assertion unit
context: Every assertion in the corpus must carry both a provenance citation (page/image-level link to the public-custodian source) and a GPS evidence rationale. The CI gates are defined in terms of a 'countable assertion unit' — the atomic record over which 100% provenance and 100% evidence-rationale completeness are measured. The mechanism for attaching provenance and evidence to assertions (named graphs + PROV-O reification vs. RDF-star) must be chosen and applied uniformly; this decision locks in what the CI gates actually count and cannot be changed mid-project without a migration.
objective: Evaluate named-graphs-plus-PROV-O reification versus RDF-star for binding provenance and evidence rationale to assertions, select one approach, define the countable assertion unit precisely (the atomic RDF statement or named-graph identifier the CI gates will enumerate), and publish the ratified decision as a short architecture decision record.
acceptanceCriteria: Two candidate mechanisms evaluated (named graphs + PROV-O vs. RDF-star): pros/cons documented for tooling support, expressiveness, and CI measurability.
One mechanism selected and ratified; the decision is binding for the project lifetime (changes require a versioned ADR and migration plan).
The countable assertion unit defined precisely: what constitutes one assertion, how it is identified, and how the CI gate enumerates and checks it for provenance and evidence-rationale completeness.
A worked example shows one real assertion (e.g., a birth-year Fact from a census record) encoded in the chosen mechanism with both the provenance block and the GPS evidence rationale attached.
Published as an architecture decision record (docs/adr/001-provenance-mechanism.md) committed via PR.
output: docs/adr/001-provenance-mechanism.md — architecture decision record ratifying the provenance+evidence mechanism and defining the countable assertion unit with a worked example, committed via PR.
